sources: Corner names: standard Spa-Francorchamps naming (e.g. Wikipedia 'Circuit de Spa-Francorchamps')
La Source technique: Coach Dave Academy / Track Titan Spa guides (brake around the 100-120 m board, late apex, exit priority for Kemmel)
Track-limit hotspots: vre-rpy zone model learned from 13 local Spa replays (2026-11-21)
Terrain at La Source (crest at turn-in, dip at apex): measured from replay elevation and tyre load

Corner cues for Eau Rouge, Les Combes, Bruxelles, No Name, Pouhon, Fagnes, Campus, Bus Stop and the La Source steering note: paraphrased from a public Popometer (Nils Naujoks) Spa GT3 coaching video, 2026-11
La Source dip and Bruxelles double-apex notes: paraphrased from S. Almeida, The Motor Racing Book Vol. 1 (II-11, II-15)

corners.name: La Source
cues: Brake around the 100-120 m board; uphill and compressing, so full pressure early is usable
Crest at turn-in unloads the car: finish braking before it
Dip at the apex loads the car: good place to go to throttle
Don't add lock past what the fronts can use: more steering here only scrubs speed; release brake to get rotation instead
The apex dip is a compression with a crest-like edge at each end: take the rotation inside the dip, expect less grip as it ends
corners.priority: exit speed for Eau Rouge / Kemmel

corners.name: Eau Rouge / Raidillon
cues: Compression at the bottom (~1060 m) adds grip; crest at the top (~1200 m) takes it away
A GT3 takes it flat: a lift here costs speed all the way down Kemmel

corners.name: Les Combes
hotspots: track-limit cut ~2300 m is judged ~11 s later (~2700 m)
cues: Brake with the left wheels on the kerb for a wider entry; the kerb strike adds rotation if you arrive 1-3 km/h quicker than feels natural

corners.name: Les Combes exit
cues: Time the upshift with the throttle lift into the right-hander: higher gear = less engine braking = a calmer rear on turn-in

corners.name: Bruxelles
cues: Delay the first apex and slow down until mid-corner; holding 40-50 % throttle mid-corner stops the rotation without accelerating
Long double-apex: GT3 (high downforce) runs a later turn-in and rounder line than a low-downforce car; don't sit on the first apex

corners.name: No Name
hotspots: track-limit cuts around 3250-3300 m are judged quickly
cues: Brake less and let the car rotate on its own: heavy brake plus big lock, then a sudden release, snaps the rear

corners.name: Pouhon
cues: Use the kerb on the right while braking; a later first apex lets you run less lock and get on power harder

corners.name: Fagnes
cues: Line up half a metre to a metre further right before the left-hander; lift and upshift together on turn-in

corners.name: Campus
cues: Sacrifice the right-hander to straighten the left-hander exit: the short straight after it is worth more

corners.name: Bus Stop
cues: Swing wide right before the left-hander so the car is rotated by mid-corner; a straight line then a late turn leaves the rotation for the exit
